title: Estradiol USP RS potency 99.9% used without the required water-content / anhydrous-basis correction
Diluent chromatogram cross-referenced as 'No Interference' in Table 2 is not peak-free; no disregard limit is defined
Specificity: 3 of 5 solution types the report says were analysed (incl. the control sample) have no reported result
Specificity shown only by spiking with 3 known impurities; no degradation samples despite the report's own definition invoking degradants
Linearity judged on correlation coefficient alone; large negative intercepts and low-end response-factor depression are never evaluated
The statistic reported as 'Co-relation Coefficient' in Tables 3 and 6 is r-squared, not the correlation coefficient the criterion specifies
Demonstrated linearity range (to 150% of individual limits) does not cover the 0.5% Total Impurities specification
Accuracy is not included as a verification parameter; the only recovery data are at a single concentration level (incl. the LOQ-specific accuracy gap vs. the method's own definition)
USP <1226> (verification of compendial procedures) is invoked for a method the report itself calls a vendor-DMF procedure distinct from the USP method
Non-compendial impurity working standards: chromatographic area-percent purity used as assigned potency, ignoring reported water content
The verification protocol and the governing SOP are referenced but never identified by number or version
The report's issue date (May 02, 2016) precedes the preparer's and QA approver's signature dates
LOD and LOQ were not derived from the standard deviation of the response as stated; both are pre-set 10%/20% dilutions of the specification level (LOQ = 2 x LOD)
No supporting data (sigma, slope, S/N, or a dilution series) is presented for the LOD/LOQ determination
Unexplained gross outlier retained in the LOD precision data set (Estradiol injection #6 = 389); it alone produces the reported 18.9% RSD
Absorptivity factors were calculated from only 3 of the 7 linearity levels (60/100/150%), and the omission is undisclosed
The absorptivity factor is strongly concentration-dependent (up to 27% spread) yet a single value is adopted with no acceptance criterion
Sensitivity solution stated as injected in §1.4.6.1 has no reported result or acceptance criterion; its area (485) is below the LOD-level mean (629)
LOQ precision is marginal for 3 of 4 analytes (within ~1.3 points of the 10% limit); no evidence the chosen LOQ level is robust
Method precision was never demonstrated for the 'Any Unspecified Impurity' and 'Total Impurities' specification attributes
Table 20 'Maximum' theoretical plates cell is wrong (11477 reported; the true maximum of the tabulated rows is 12601)
Unspecified impurity of 0.15% is reported as meeting the NMT 0.10% limit in the equivalency study, and the section concludes equivalency
The two methods are not 'comparable' for the single largest unspecified impurity: 0.15% by USP method vs. not detected in-house
Table 19 is internally inconsistent for the USP method: total impurities (0.14%) is lower than the single largest unspecified impurity (0.15%)
The §1.4.7 conclusion asserts solutions were 'stored at room temperature,' a condition documented nowhere in the study description
§1.5 Conclusions omits Limit of Detection, Limit of Quantitation, Absorptivity Factor, and System Suitability while claiming complete coverage
§1.4.9's conclusion claims system suitability across the 'entire verification study' but Table 20 omits the solution-stability runs
Table 17's notebook-page citation differs between the report body (Notebook 8133, p.56) and Table 1 (Notebook 8133, p.46)
